key_insight: Large language models can be guided to predict the exact structural edits needed to turn hard-to-synthesize molecules into more synthesizable ones. This improves synthesizability while better preserving the molecule’s useful core features than traditional optimization methods.
problem_solved: Computational drug design often proposes molecules that look promising on paper but are too difficult or impractical to synthesize in the lab. The paper addresses how to efficiently revise these molecules so they become more synthetically feasible without losing key properties.
method: Use a large language model to predict edit sequences rather than generating entirely new molecules from scratch.
Model molecule improvement as a stepwise structural editing task aimed at synthesizability optimization.
Compare against traditional approaches and show better performance in preserving important molecular features while improving synthetic accessibility.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners in chemistry, this offers a practical way to make generative models more useful in real-world drug discovery. It shifts optimization from unconstrained molecule generation to targeted, interpretable edits that are easier to validate and synthesize.

paper_title: Guiding large language models to predict edit sequences for molecular synthesizability optimization
